newsitem.title: USA: NY Power might sell up to $4.2 bln of taxable debt.
newsitem.headline: NY Power might sell up to $4.2 bln of taxable debt.

text.p: The New York State Power Authority, which has proposed buying bulk transmission sytems from investor-owned untilities, said on Tuesday that if its plan were approved, it could sell up to $4.2 billion of taxable debt.

Wes Collins, the Authority's treasurer, explained the Authority was willing to pay a premium of as much as 50 percent to 100 percent over the assets' book value, which on a statewide basis is estimated at $1.5 billion to $2.2 billion.

"We would be issuing $4.2 billion of debt," he said, assuming the maximum amount were paid for the transmission facilities. The bonds would be taxable, said Collins, who spoke at a Bond Buyer conference on New York Public Finance Conference here.

The capital gain on the premiums could be offset by losses on contract settlements with independent power producers, the official said, saying this would take care of the federal taxes that otherwise might be due.

The state power authority estimates its plan could produce as much as $3 billion of savings over five years, as the agency has lower borrowing costs, and could stretch out contracts with independent power producers and negotiate discounts with them, Collins said.
The New York Power Authority's proposal is expected to be acted upon by the Public Service Commission in "the first part" of 1997, Collins said.

"We give this proposal about a 50 percent chance of happening," he said. He added that while utilities are free to approach the Authority individually to negotiate such sales, the state legislature also could authorize the Authority to go ahead with the voluntary program.
